This causes a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which shorter wavelengths—like blue and violet—are scattered far more strongly than longer wavelengths like red. Although violet light scatters even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue, and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so the sky appears blue.
